methods.text: Change one variable at a time and record each result.
Build the part you understand least first.
Keep a one-line log of every decision and the reason for it.
Name the worst version you would still ship, and hold that as the floor.
Stop each session mid-step so the next one starts easily.
Price each feature in hours before building it, and drop the dearest one.
Write down the result you expect before each test, then compare.
Read every line of text aloud and cut what you stumble on.

constraints.text: Every input rejects impossible values with a plain message.
Works at 200 percent browser zoom without horizontal scrolling.

tasks.text: Churn cost calculator: the buyer's customer count, monthly loss rate, and value per customer give revenue lost per year and what one point less churn would keep.
Error cost estimator: cases per month, error rate, and cost to fix each error give the monthly cost of mistakes and the saving at a lower rate the buyer sets.
Handover map: the buyer's tasks and the owner of each give a table of handoffs between people and a list of steps with no clear owner.
Late payment cost: invoices with amounts and days overdue give the cash tied up, the cost of waiting at a rate the buyer sets, and the oldest balances.
Rollout calendar: a start date and the buyer's teams or sites give a staggered dated schedule, with any overlapping weeks marked.
Tool overlap finder: the buyer's current tools with cost and main uses give the uses covered twice and the yearly spend on that overlap.

methods: Design the error and empty states first.
List the assumptions in the brief and check each one.
Make it work in black and white before adding color.
Take the conventions of a genre and break exactly one.
Write the copy before the layout.
Scope the work to what fits in one day.
constraints: Under 100 words of fixed text on the page.
tasks: Cost-of-inaction calculator: the buyer's current volumes and rates give what the problem costs per month and per year, with each step of the sum shown.
Readiness scorecard: twelve yes-or-no questions give a score out of 100, the three weakest areas, and one next step for each.
Benchmark checker: the buyer's own figures sit next to typical ranges they can edit, with each gap marked ahead, level, or behind.
Leak finder: a funnel of stages with counts gives the stage that loses the most and what fixing half of that loss would be worth.
Time-back calculator: weekly hours on manual tasks and an hourly cost give the hours and money an automated step would return.
Before-and-after map: today's process as a list of steps becomes a side-by-side view marking the steps that could be removed or automated.
